inspector.purpose_summary: A single-file Python governance kernel (ANVIL.py, 69KB, 63 top-level classes, standard-library-only imports) whose module docstring names it 'GSA Governance Adapter v2.1' and which implements SHA-256 canonical hashing and chain verification (IntegrityEngine, ChainVerifier, IntegrityManager), frozen/immutable envelopes (deep_freeze, GsaContextEnvelope), a module registry and loader, a DAG lineage with named checkpoints (GovernanceDag, CheckpointRegistry), audit/telemetry/event-bus/health services, an OscillationDetector, and a GsaKernel entry point. Alongside it is anvil_validation_harness.py, a custom (non-pytest) runner that exec()s ANVIL.py and records PASS/FAIL/FINDING across six buckets (enforcement, integrity chain, immutability, registry rules, round-trip, oscillation), plus a .ghost_baseline.json of 21 suppressed static-analysis findings from a tool called ghost_buster. There is no packaging manifest, no tests/ directory, no CI, and no conversation or transcript content of any kind.
inspector.eligibility_rationale: The repository's content is source code, a validation harness, a static-analysis baseline, a README and an Apache-2.0 LICENSE. Nothing in any file is conversation history, chat history, or transcript material; the sole exclusion criterion does not apply. Commit messages carry Claude co-author trailers and session links, but that is authorship metadata, not stored conversation content.

inspector.purpose_summary: The repository archives one AI-assistant conversation (TRANSCRIPT.md, 340 KB, described by PROVENANCE.md as a 9-turn Gemini transcript) together with the eight distinct JSON payloads the user pasted as prompts in that conversation (artifact_1/2/3/5/6/7/8/9.json, ~237 KB), each a 'code_modules/segments/workflows/architecture/risks/notes/commands' data object. A later pass (commits 3ef97b3, 617d767, c5e7a96) pulled the code_modules[].body strings out of those payloads into 42 individually named, verbatim, deliberately unrepaired .py fragment files plus one JSON under extracted/report_N/, and the README documents a cross-reference of those fragments against sibling repos (what was kept, removed as duplicate, or moved to FORTRESS). There is no processing tooling, no manifest, no CI, and no runnable test suite in the repo; the extracted code is a specimen corpus of corrupted, non-runnable fragments, not a working system.
inspector.eligibility_rationale: Two readings compete. (a) Every byte of substantive content originates from a single conversation: the transcript itself, the prompt payloads sliced out of it, and code strings sliced out of those payloads; the initial commit is 'Archive of pre-existing artifact. Preserved verbatim, unmodified' and the description calls it 'One archived Gemini transcript' - which points to CONVERSATION_OR_TRANSCRIPT_ARCHIVE / exclusion. (b) The repo's README, the three extraction/cross-reference commits, and the .ghost_archive marker ('Extracted reports and recovered fragments, kept as a record') frame its current purpose as a specimen corpus of recovered code fragments (older snapshots of ClaudeGovernanceDecider/IcebergProductionHarness with claimed drift from GSA-815/sentinel_os, standalone filter classes claimed absent elsewhere, the UGPISOmegaController integration blueprint) explicitly cross-referenced to at least 8 other corpus repos - which is specimen/data-corpus evidence that the rules say is ELIGIBLE. It contains no extraction pipeline or analysis code, so it is not the tooling case either. Because the sole exclusion criterion is 'primary purpose is storing conversation history' and the observed primary use has shifted to curating recovered code specimens with cross-repo provenance, I do not exclude it; the ambiguity is recorded for the investigator.

inspector.purpose_summary: By volume the repository is a ChatGPT conversation-history archive: one raw account data export (conversations-000..008.json plus catalogue files, ~95 MB), per-message derivatives (data/raw.jsonl 53.8 MB, data/raw.csv 49.7 MB), a 555 KB catalogue (index/manifest.json), and per-conversation Markdown transcripts and deterministic summaries (README/PROVENANCE claim 863 each; full listings observed but not hand-counted). Alongside that it carries substantive tooling: a real, re-runnable extraction pipeline with credential and phrase redaction that also generates the manifest (scripts/process.py, 17 KB, fully inspected), a standalone PII redactor with dry-run/verify/audit modes (tools/redact_pii.py, 12 KB, fully inspected) plus its operating procedure (tools/REDACTION.md), and a derived forensic package (derived/round2_governance_gateway/, 13 files) that reconstructs an adversarial-testing campaign against the corpus repo Governance_Gateway from a single conversation, including two executable reproduction scripts and two extracted attack-source files, and is explicitly framed as white-paper source material. A non-default branch (claude/systems-repos-history-audit-k1ufhe) adds derived/cross_archive/SYSTEM_AND_REPO_INVENTORY.md, a cross-archive inventory of every system and repository named across the account's five history archives.
inspector.eligibility_rationale: The dominant content is conversation history, which on its own would meet the sole exclusion criterion. But the repo also contains an extraction/processing pipeline, redaction tooling, a manifest generator, a forensic analysis + reproduction package aimed at another corpus repo, and (on a branch) a cross-repo inventory. The rules state that transcripts plus substantive tooling is MIXED_AMBIGUOUS → AMBIGUOUS_INVESTIGATE; it is not excluded and the ambiguity is recorded. The derived package and the branch inventory are in addition direct evidence about other corpus repos (Governance_Gateway, HERALD, Conservation_Kernel, and the 41+15 repos catalogued).

inspector.purpose_summary: The repository self-describes (README.md, PROVENANCE.md) as an archive of one single-turn Gemini transcript (TRANSCRIPT.md) in which a user pasted a small Python module, 'CITADEL v1.1', a regex-based LLM-output enforcement engine (identity/hedging/passive/causality/em-dash detection, scoring, rewriting), and the AI returned a prose audit. Beyond the transcript it holds four Python files: artifact_1.py (the pasted module, two near-identical drafts concatenated, now in formatted multi-line form on main), two readable per-draft splits (citadel_v1.1_copy1.py, citadel_v1.1_copy2.py), and citadel_v1.2.py, an authored post-archival extension adding a 'prohibited_verbs' check said to be salvaged from the deleted STRIDE repo. There are no tests, no manifests, no CI, and a single flat directory; Apache-2.0 LICENSE and a detailed PROVENANCE.md are present.
inspector.eligibility_rationale: The repo's declared primary purpose is archiving one AI transcript, which touches the sole exclusion criterion, but it is a single-turn archive whose artifact is a code system, and it additionally contains substantive non-transcript content: readable reconstructions of the engine and a v1.2 extension with new functionality wired through Constraint/PROFILES/PENALTY/detect()/rewrite(). By byte count the Python code (~44.5 KB across 4 files) exceeds the transcript (18 KB). It is not a bulk chat-history store like a *_History repo. Per the rules, a transcript store that also contains substantive code is MIXED_AMBIGUOUS and must be investigated, not excluded.

inspector.purpose_summary: The repository is, by volume, a private archive of a Claude.ai account data export: a raw vendor export split into ~265 per-conversation JSON files plus memories/projects/reflections, and derived per-conversation Markdown transcripts, paired naive-keyword and export-supplied AI summaries, per-conversation flattened JSONL rows, and a JSON manifest. Alongside the data it carries two real Python tools: scripts/process.py (a ~190-line re-runnable extraction pipeline that generates the transcripts, summaries, manifest and raw JSONL from the export) and tools/redact_pii.py (a ~330-line deterministic PII redactor with dry-run, verify and audit modes, ported from the ChatGPT_History repo and, per its own commit message, not yet run on this repo's data). There are no tests, no CI, no dependency manifests; the notebook is a one-cell stub. A .ghost_archive marker declares 'An export of Claude conversations, kept as data. Nothing here runs.'
inspector.eligibility_rationale: The dominant content is a conversation/transcript archive (the sole exclusion criterion), but the repo also contains substantive tooling as defined by the rules: an extraction/processing pipeline that is also the manifest generator (scripts/process.py) and a separate PII-redaction tool with a documented procedure (tools/redact_pii.py, tools/REDACTION.md). Per the rule that transcripts plus substantive tooling is MIXED_AMBIGUOUS, this is AMBIGUOUS_INVESTIGATE rather than excluded. The ambiguity is genuine: the tooling is small (2 Python files, ~20 KB) relative to ~1,300 data files and ~149 MB, and the repo's own archive marker asserts nothing runs, while the README and commit messages assert the pipeline is real and re-runnable.

Alongside the transcript it holds the code payload extracted from that transcript: a 1,153-line reconstructed (unflattened) Python file content-pipeline-user-source.py added on 2026-09-11 by PR #2 with a header stating it was rebuilt by 'ghost_tools' unflattener', the original flattened bytes as content-pipeline-user-source.py.flattened, and a 3.7 KB content-pipeline-modularized.txt holding the AI's ContentPolishPipeline module plus an empty governance_filters.py header (its first line 'Module: content_pipelines.py | Version: v1.0.0' is not valid Python). PROVENANCE.md and README.md document the extraction, the non-executing status, and cross-repo migrations of classes out of this repo into EDDP, GSA-GATEWAY, GSA-815 and GRAPH; business-strategy-notes.md is a verbatim reformatted extract of transcript turns 2-6. There are no manifests, tests, CI, scripts or subdirectories.
inspector.eligibility_rationale: The README and the repo's own description declare the primary purpose as preserving a single AI chat transcript, and TRANSCRIPT.md is the largest file (39% of bytes), which points toward the conversation-archive exclusion. However the repo is not a bulk chat-history dump: it holds a single transcript treated as provenance for code specimens (~45% of bytes are Python-text artifacts, including a reconstructed 1,153-line .py file added by tooling from another corpus repo on 2026-09-11), it has a 10-commit working history of renames, trims, cross-repo class migrations and two merged PRs, and README/PROVENANCE document it as the origin of code now living in EDDP, GSA-GATEWAY, GSA-815, GRAPH and content-polish-pipeline. Those code specimens and cross-repo links are forensic evidence beyond conversation history, so per the rules the ambiguity is recorded rather than the repo excluded. A reviewer could reasonably argue either way; not excluded on this pass.

It ships one pytest file, one demo script, a GitHub Actions CI matrix (Python 3.10-3.13), and two long-form provenance documents stating the code is a September 2026 reconstruction from a Gemini conversation export after the original repository was lost. The single commit is authored 'Claude' with a Claude-Session trailer.
inspector.eligibility_rationale: The repository's primary content is source code plus tests, CI, and manifests. It does not store conversation history or transcripts; it only references transcripts held in other repos (Gemini_History, Gemini_Extraction) as provenance. The sole exclusion criterion (primary purpose = conversation archive) does not apply.

inspector.purpose_summary: Ecology is a Python RAG / "living memory" prototype: root-level modules (ecology.py, rag_engine.py, history_loader.py, semantic_index.py, lexical_index.py, containment.py, finding.py, code_scanner.py, preprocess.py, polish_bridge.py) plus a src/ package (rag, governance, telemetry), 9 ingestion/DB scripts, and a 12-subdirectory pytest suite (~35 test files) gated by a GitHub Actions workflow running pytest and ruff. It carries a large harvested data directory corpus/ (~360 files of mixed/unrecorded origin, including an 18MB synapsis-master.zip and many *.md/*.py exports from other repos, documented in corpus/PROVENANCE.md and corpus/ORIGIN.tsv) and raw_sources/ (one 1.28MB PDF export of a Gemini chat, per PROVENANCE.md "PDF exports of chat transcripts"). history_loader.py is explicitly a reader for the Claude_History/ChatGPT_History/CoPilot_History/Gemini_History archives, so the tool is built to ingest conversation history, but the repo itself stores tooling plus a harvested code/doc corpus rather than being primarily a transcript archive.
inspector.eligibility_rationale: The dominant purpose observed is a substantive system (RAG engine, tests, CI, scripts, license, provenance ledger), which would make it ELIGIBLE outright. However it also contains raw_sources/ (a PDF chat-transcript export, per corpus/PROVENANCE.md) and a large harvested corpus/ directory of exported material from other systems and conversations, and its core ingestion path (history_loader.py) targets the *_History conversation archives. Per the rule that a repository with transcripts AND substantive tooling is MIXED_AMBIGUOUS, eligibility is AMBIGUOUS_INVESTIGATE. It should not be excluded: the conversation-archive material is a minority of the repo by file count and the primary purpose is the tooling.

inspector.purpose_summary: The repository holds six runnable-looking Python modules (an integrated fail-closed pipeline orchestrator, a telemetry guardrail, an HMAC ingestion-authentication module, an 8-module assessment/dispatch adapter, and two standalone 'core engine' reference files), two flattened archived source payloads under _archive/, a detailed PROVENANCE.md, and a 464 KB TRANSCRIPT.md that PROVENANCE.md describes as the verbatim 14-turn Gemini conversation from which the code was extracted. By byte count the repo is dominated by the conversation transcript; by file count and by the README's stated purpose it is a preservation archive of code artifacts with shared provenance, plus a small pipeline that was later wired together from them. Commit history shows the repo briefly hosted a prototype conversation-history SQLite database (data/, generated/, notebooks/, scripts/, index/) that was deleted on 2026-08-19 as unrelated; that history likely explains the 10 MB reported size versus ~560 KB of visible content. Two non-default branches (claude/parses, claude/recovered-originals) contain a September 2026 recovery pass over the flattened _archive files.
inspector.eligibility_rationale: Stores a large verbatim AI-conversation transcript (TRANSCRIPT.md) AND substantive code (six Python modules including an orchestrator that imports and composes three of them, inspected in eddp_pipeline.py), plus a provenance record. Per the rules, transcript storage combined with substantive tooling is MIXED_AMBIGUOUS, not excluded. The README frames the primary purpose as artifact preservation/forensic reconstruction rather than conversation archiving, and the earlier conversation-database prototype was explicitly removed, which leans toward eligible, but the transcript is the majority of the bytes so the ambiguity is recorded rather than resolved here.

inspector.eligibility_rationale: Every self-description observed (README.md, .ghost_archive, commit messages) frames this as an AI-assistant (Gemini) activity/conversation archive, which is the sole exclusion criterion. Under the stated rule that transcript storage plus tooling is MIXED_AMBIGUOUS and must not be excluded, the repo is flagged for investigation rather than excluded. If the investigator applies the exclusion strictly on declared purpose, the case for EXCLUDED_CONVERSATION_ARCHIVE is: the README's stated intent is a 'queryable conversation archive' and the only substantive code was ported from elsewhere and never executed here.

inspector.purpose_summary: A dependency-free Python 3.11 package (triad42, version 2.2.0 per pyproject.toml) implementing an advisory review harness that enforces procedural rules for a Red/Gray/Green/42 review: stage order, epistemic labels with human-authorized relabelling, severity floors and 1/2/3 cluster escalation, two-phase Gray, Green break statements, a five-check 42 novelty gate, provenance (origin vs support, human-root requirement, erasure cascade), an append-only candidate store, plus three bounded add-on modules (integrity, telemetry, observations). A ghost_buster baseline JSON is committed. No conversation or transcript content was observed.

enumeration.description: An advisory harness that governs a four-stage review — Red (adversarial), Gray (structural), Green (real-world grounding), 42 (novelty synthesis) — enforcing stage order, epistemic labels, severity accumulation, and append-only provenance.
